summary.prose: When the assistant changes files during a chat turn, the dev chat shows each changed section of each file as its own widget: the path, the lines added and removed, line numbers and the theme's diff colours, cut to 8 lines until the reader opens it. The plugin gets the sections by asking git, after every tool call, how the working tree differs from the snapshot it took when the turn started, so the same thing happens for claude and for codex, whether the change was made by an edit tool or by a shell command. A section that changes again updates its widget in place, and the widgets are saved with the chat so they are still there, in their latest form, after a reload. This replaces the diff box that is squashed to nothing today, and the bare path line and 'file has been updated' line that are all the reader sees; an edit that produces no widget still shows its path line. One limit: if the reader switches chat, closes the panel or reloads the window while a turn is running, the rest of that turn shows path lines as today, not widgets.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Show each changed section of a turn's git diff as a widget in the dev chat

api.name: createGitBaseline
api.signature: createGitBaseline(deps: GitBaselineDeps): WorkspaceBaseline  // WorkspaceBaseline gains changes(handle: BaselineHandle): Promise<string | undefined> and release(handle: BaselineHandle): Promise<void>; BaselineHandle gains readonly index?: string; GitBaselineDeps.runGit gains a third argument env?: Record<string, string>; GitBaselineDeps gains tempIndexPath(): string, copyFile(from: string, to: string): Promise<boolean>, removeFile(path: string): Promise<void>

parameters.name: deps.runGit
parameters.type: (cwd: string, args: string[], env?: Record<string, string>) => Promise<{ ok: boolean; stdout: string }>
parameters.purpose: Runs git in cwd; env is added to the process environment (used for GIT_INDEX_FILE). Never rejects.

parameters.name: deps.tempIndexPath
parameters.purpose: A fresh absolute path in the system temporary directory for one turn's private index file.

parameters.name: deps.copyFile
parameters.purpose: Copies the repository's index to the private path; false when the source does not exist or cannot be read.

parameters.name: deps.removeFile
parameters.purpose: Removes the private index (and its lock file if one is left); a missing file is not an error.

returns.meaning: snapshot(cwd): asks `git rev-parse --git-path index` for the index path, resolves the printed path against cwd with deps.toAbs (git prints it relative to the directory it ran in), copies that file to tempIndexPath(), runs `git add -A --ignore-errors` and then `git write-tree` with GIT_INDEX_FILE set to the copy, and returns { ref: <tree id>, index: <the copy's path> }. The tree holds tracked and untracked files and no ignored ones; the user's own index is not written. When the copy reports false, git starts from an empty private index and the snapshot still works. changes(handle): runs the same add and write-tree against handle.index, returns '' when the new tree id equals handle.ref, otherwise the stdout of `git -c core.quotepath=false diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-renames -U3 --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ --relative <handle.ref> <new tree>`; undefined when write-tree or diff fails. read(handle, path): `git show <handle.ref>:./<rel>` as today, now against a tree id; the separate list of untracked files' text is removed because the tree holds those files. release(handle): removes handle.index.

errors.condition: `git write-tree` fails or prints no tree id. The governor catches it and the turn runs with no snapshot, as it does today when the snapshot fails.

preconditions: available(cwd) returned true (cwd is inside a git work tree)
postconditions: The repository's own index file and `git status` are the same before and after snapshot and changes
`git add` exiting non-zero does not fail snapshot or changes; only write-tree's result decides
changes returns paths relative to cwd and nothing for a change outside cwd

api.name: createEditGovernor
api.signature: createEditGovernor(deps: EditGovernorDeps): EditGovernor  // EditGovernor gains sectionsActive(): boolean, check(): Promise<void>, sectionPaths(): ReadonlySet<string> and abandonTurn(): Promise<void>; EditRenderSeam loses showChat and gains showSections(ops: readonly SectionOp[], overflow: { sections: number; files: number } | undefined): void and sectionsUnreadable(): void; EditGovernorDeps loses computeDiff

parameters.name: deps.render.showSections
parameters.type: (ops: readonly SectionOp[], overflow: { sections: number; files: number } | undefined) => void
parameters.purpose: Receives the result of one check: sections to add, update and withdraw, and how many new sections the per-check limit left out.

parameters.name: deps.render.sectionsUnreadable
parameters.purpose: Called at most once per turn, the first time a check cannot read the changes.

returns.meaning: sectionsActive(): true when the current turn has a snapshot handle and diffView() is 'chat'. check(): when sectionsActive(), asks baseline.changes for the patch, parses it with parsePatch and reconciles it with the sections known for this turn with reconcileSections (both in the new diff-sections.ts), then calls render.showSections when there is at least one operation or an overflow. Checks run one at a time: a call made while a check runs sets a flag and one more check runs when the current one ends; the promise of every such call resolves when a check that started after the call has ended. sectionPaths(): the cwd-relative paths of every section known this turn, shown or hidden. observe(path): acts only when diffView() is 'editor': it reads the turn-start content, tracks the edit for decide when the mode is review, and calls showEditor, all as today; in the chat view it does nothing. decide is unchanged. beginTurn: releases the previous turn's handle before taking the new snapshot and clears the known sections. resolveTurn: runs one last check, waits for it, then calls baseline.release. abandonTurn: ends the turn's checks without a last one: it clears the snapshot handle and the known sections at once, so sectionsActive() is false and a check still in flight calls nothing on the render seam, then calls baseline.release.

postconditions: A check that ends after a newer turn began, or after abandonTurn, calls nothing on the render seam
No method of the governor rejects; a failure is logged through deps.logger
defaultComputeDiff is removed from edit-governor.ts, and computeDiff from ChatEditGovernanceDeps and from the object extension.ts passes

api.name: createChatPanelHost
api.signature: createChatPanelHost(deps: ChatPanelHostDeps): ChatPanelHost  // unchanged signature; ChatEditGovernanceDeps loses computeDiff and gains relPath(path: string): string

parameters.name: deps.editGovernance.relPath
parameters.purpose: An edit event's path as git names it: relative to the workspace folder, with forward slashes (extension.ts passes its relForGit over the chat folder).

returns.meaning: THE TURN'S DIFF STATE. The host makes one object for each turn it starts, in that turn's beforeRun after governor.beginTurn, when governor.sectionsActive() is true. It holds the session, a key made once (the host's clock in milliseconds in base 36 and a counter), the sid of each section, the held paths and whether it has ended. Only the sink of that turn (the onEvent and onTerminal that runTurn passes to turns.start) uses it. A turn with no such object, and every followed turn (followLiveTurn, the other caller of appendEvent), writes and posts every row as today and asks for no check, whatever the governor holds. ROWS. Rows are only ever pushed. showSections, for the diff state that is open: 'add' pushes a role:'diff' row with sid = the key plus the section id, unique in the transcript; 'update' pushes a role:'diff' row with the new content and replaces: <that sid>; 'withdraw' pushes a role:'diff' row with replaces, withdrawn:true and no lines. An overflow pushes a marker row with the edit marker class and the text '<n> more changed sections in <m> files are not shown'. sectionsUnreadable pushes a marker row 'The changes of this turn could not be read'. Each such row, a diff row or a marker row, is posted as { type:'transcript-row', rowIndex, row } while the panel is not disposed and that session is the one shown. HELD PATHS. While its diff state is open, the turn's sink: on a 'file-edit' event writes no marker row and posts nothing, and holds the path; on a 'tool-result' event with editPath and without isError writes no row and posts nothing; on a 'tool-result' event with editPath and isError pushes and posts the held path's marker row (through 'transcript-row') and then the result row as today. A held path is settled after the check that follows the end of its edit: for a 'file-edit' event with applied:true (codex) the check asked for at that event, for a claude edit the check asked for at its successful result. Settling pushes and posts the path's marker row (the row appendEvent writes for a 'file-edit' event today) when governor.sectionPaths() does not contain relPath(path), and nothing otherwise. governor.check() is called after every 'file-edit' and every 'tool-result' event of that sink and is never awaited by the turn loop. ENDING. The diff state is ended once, by whichever comes first: (a) the turn's onTerminal: governor.resolveTurn() runs the last check, then every path still held is settled and the session is saved; (b) any other way the turn stops reporting to its sink: the host ends the open diff state before each call of turns.detach() (a chat switch, the panel closing, adopt) and of turns.stop(), in the sink's onError, and at the top of the next turn's beforeRun before governor.beginTurn. In (b) every held path is settled at once against governor.sectionPaths() as it stands, the session is saved and governor.abandonTurn() is called. After the diff state has ended, a result of a check still in flight is dropped (nothing is pushed or posted) and any later event of that sink is written as today.

postconditions: An edit seen while a diff state is open ends as at least one of: a widget for its path, its path's marker row, or its error row, on every way the turn can stop reporting
No diff state and no snapshot outlives its turn's sink: both are ended at the turn's end, a detach, a stop, an error or the next turn's start
The 'edit-prompt' message is removed from the protocol, and the shell's renderDiff function and the seven .insrc-diff-* rules are removed; the widget's root keeps the class insrc-term-diff
The 'edit-decision' message, governor.decide, followLiveTurn and the turn lifecycle are left as they are
The transcript element's children do not shrink: the shell carries `#insrc-term>*{flex-shrink:0;}`

api.name: toViewModel
api.signature: toViewModel(entry: TranscriptEntry | TurnEvent): RowViewModel  // RowViewModel.kind gains 'diff'

parameters.name: entry
parameters.purpose: A saved row or a live event.

returns.meaning: A role:'diff' row maps to { kind:'diff', text: row.path, collapsible:false, meta:{ the row's fields } }, in the host function and in its webview mirror. A tool-result view-model is collapsible only when its output is long by the registry's isLong rule (more than 3 lines or 240 characters); a short output is drawn plain with no chevron. The registry registers a 'diff' renderer that, like the other saved kinds, builds its node through line() so it is appended on the live path, on restore and on an older page, and remembers the node under the row's sid. A row with `replaces` or `withdrawn` draws nothing and appends nothing. Otherwise the node is the widget of docs/mocks/chat-diff-widget.html, with the root class insrc-term-diff: a header (chevron, edit glyph, path cut at the front, 'new file' / 'deleted' / 'binary file' when it applies, +added and −removed), then one line per diff line with its line number (the old number for a removed line, the new number otherwise), sign and text; the first 8 lines show, and a 'show N more lines' / 'show less' button and the header toggle the rest; a section of 8 lines or fewer has no chevron and no button; a row with omitted > 0 ends with '<omitted> more lines not saved' when open; a binary row shows 'binary file changed'. The registry also returns redrawDiff(row): it finds the widget remembered under row.replaces, rebuilds its content from the row, keeps it open if it was open, hides it when the row is withdrawn, and does nothing when no widget is remembered under that id. The remembered widgets are forgotten when the registry's keys are reset and when the pager drops their nodes.

postconditions: The host toViewModel and the webview mirror give the same view-model for a diff row (the existing parity test covers the new kind)
The diff renderer writes text with textContent only and names only the shell's theme names

dataModelChanges.details: One section of one file's diff: { path: string; oldStart: number; oldLines: number; newStart: number; newLines: number; added: number; removed: number; lines: string[]; omitted?: number; binary?: true; fileState?: 'new' | 'deleted' }. The module is pure and exports: MAX_SECTION_LINES = 400, MAX_NEW_SECTIONS_PER_CHECK = 20, COLLAPSED_LINES = 8; parsePatch(patch: string): DiffSection[] (one entry per @@ section; a file with a 'Binary files' line gives one entry with binary:true and no lines; the path is read from the '+++ b/' line, or the '--- a/' line for a deleted file, or the 'diff --git' line for a binary file, with a trailing tab dropped and a quoted name unquoted; lines beyond 400 are dropped and counted in omitted while added and removed count the whole section; a '\ No newline at end of file' line is kept and counted as neither); SectionOp = { op:'add'; id: number; section: DiffSection } | { op:'update'; id: number; section: DiffSection } | { op:'withdraw'; id: number }; KnownSection = { id: number; section: DiffSection; shown: boolean }; reconcileSections(known: readonly KnownSection[], next: readonly DiffSection[], nextId: number, limit?: number): { ops: SectionOp[]; known: KnownSection[]; nextId: number; overflow: { sections: number; files: number } | undefined }. Matching: within one path, a next section takes the lowest-id known section not yet taken whose old-line range overlaps its own (range = oldStart to oldStart + max(oldLines, 1) - 1; a binary section matches the path's binary section); equal content gives no operation, different content gives 'update'; a known section taken by no next section gives 'withdraw' and is dropped; a next section that takes none gives 'add' until the limit is reached in this call, after which it is kept as known with shown:false and counted in overflow. A known section with shown:false never produces an operation.

A new variant: { role:'diff'; sid?: string; replaces?: string; path; oldStart; oldLines; newStart; newLines; added; removed; lines: readonly string[]; omitted?: number; binary?: true; fileState?: 'new' | 'deleted'; withdrawn?: true; at: string }. The first row of a section carries sid, unique in the transcript; a later version of the section carries replaces with that sid and no sid of its own, and is never drawn at its own place. The link does not use row positions, which the file store does not keep stable when another window appends to the same session. Rows are only pushed, as the file store requires; session-file-store.ts and session-store.ts need no change beyond the type. Existing variants and saved sessions are unchanged.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: + | { readonly role: 'diff'; readonly sid?: string; readonly replaces?: string; readonly path: string; readonly oldStart: number; readonly oldLines: number; readonly newStart: number; readonly newLines: number; readonly added: number; readonly removed: number; readonly lines: readonly string[]; readonly omitted?: number; readonly binary?: true; readonly fileState?: 'new' | 'deleted'; readonly withdrawn?: true; readonly at: string }

dataModelChanges.entity: TurnEvent 'tool-result' and 'file-edit', and the adapter's mappers
dataModelChanges.details: Live-only optional fields, none saved. On 'tool-result': editPath?: string (the file_path of the claude Edit or Write call this result answers; the adapter remembers those tool_use ids as it remembers commands) and isError?: boolean (true when the claude tool_result block has is_error true). On 'file-edit': applied?: true, set by the codex mapper, whose event is emitted when the change is done; the claude mapper leaves it out because its event is emitted when the call is made. The codex mapper changes with it: a completed file_change item emits one 'file-edit' event per entry of item.changes, with that entry's path; an item with no changes list but with a path emits one event with it; an item with neither emits one event with the path '(unknown)' as today. CLAUDE_EDIT_TOOLS stays Edit and Write: a call of any other tool keeps its tool-call row and its result row, and what it changed shows as widgets after the check that follows its result.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff:
tool-result: + readonly editPath?: string; + readonly isError?: boolean;
file-edit:   + readonly applied?: true;

dataModelChanges.details: 'edit-prompt' is removed and { type:'transcript-row'; rowIndex: number; row: TranscriptEntry } is added; the invariant that every host message kind is listed in the protocol's kind list stays, with 'transcript-row' in place of 'edit-prompt'. It carries a row the host pushed outside the event path: a diff row, or a marker row (the overflow line, the unreadable line, a settled path line, the path line before a failed edit's error). The shell handles it inside pager.track(rowIndex, ...): for a role:'diff' row with `replaces` it calls reg.redrawDiff(row); for any other row it calls reg.renderRow(reg.toViewModel(row)), which appends the widget or the marker line through line(). A marker row drawn this way and the same row drawn on restore go through the same toViewModel mapping.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff:
- | { type: 'edit-prompt'; path: string; diff: UnifiedDiff; review?: boolean }
+ | { type: 'transcript-row'; rowIndex: number; row: TranscriptEntry }

errorCases.scenario: The workspace folder is not inside a git repository
errorCases.detection: baseline.available(cwd) returns false in beginTurn, so the turn has no snapshot handle, sectionsActive() is false and the host makes no diff state for the turn
errorCases.response: No check runs and no row is held back: the path line and the tool result row are written as today
errorCases.userImpact: No widgets; the reader sees what they see today

errorCases.scenario: The snapshot fails at turn start (write-tree fails, git missing, the temporary directory is not writable)
errorCases.detection: snapshot throws; the governor's safe wrapper logs it and leaves the handle undefined
errorCases.response: The turn runs as in a folder with no repository; the private index file, if one was made, is removed
errorCases.userImpact: No widgets for this turn; the path lines show as today

errorCases.scenario: A check cannot read the changes (write-tree or diff fails, or the patch is larger than the runner's 64 MB buffer)
errorCases.response: The governor logs a warning and calls render.sectionsUnreadable() the first time in the turn; later checks still run and can succeed. Known sections are kept. A path held for that check is settled as usual, so its path line is written when it has no section
errorCases.userImpact: One line 'The changes of this turn could not be read' and the path lines of the edits; widgets already drawn stay

errorCases.scenario: The patch has a part the parser does not understand
errorCases.detection: parsePatch meets a line that is not a file header, a section header or a diff line where one is expected
errorCases.response: The parser skips to the next 'diff --git' line and keeps every section it read; it never throws
errorCases.userImpact: The unreadable file has no widget; if it was edited by an edit tool its path line shows; the others show

errorCases.scenario: The turn is detached in mid-turn: the reader switches chat, closes the panel, or the host adopts another session
errorCases.detection: The host is about to call turns.detach() and a diff state is open
errorCases.response: Before the call the host ends the diff state: every held path is settled at once against governor.sectionPaths(), the session is saved (the lifecycle's detach saves it again with the cursor) and governor.abandonTurn() releases the snapshot. The lifecycle then stops calling the sink without onTerminal, as today
errorCases.userImpact: The widgets drawn so far stay. A file whose edit was pending shows its path line. When the reader comes back, the rest of the turn is followed and shows path lines and result rows as today, with no widgets

errorCases.scenario: The turn is stopped with the Stop control
errorCases.detection: The host is about to call turns.stop() and a diff state is open
errorCases.response: The diff state is ended as for a detach. If the lifecycle then calls onTerminal, the diff state has already ended and onTerminal writes and saves as today
errorCases.userImpact: The widgets drawn so far stay; a pending edit shows its path line

errorCases.scenario: A newer turn starts while an older one has not reached its end (the newest message wins)
errorCases.detection: The newer turn's beforeRun finds a diff state still open
errorCases.response: It ends that diff state as for a detach, before governor.beginTurn takes the new snapshot. The lifecycle no longer calls the older sink
errorCases.userImpact: The older turn's widgets stay and its pending edits show their path lines, before the new turn's rows

errorCases.scenario: The turn's sink or the adapter throws
errorCases.detection: The lifecycle calls the sink's onError instead of onTerminal
errorCases.response: onError ends the open diff state as for a detach, then posts the error as today
errorCases.userImpact: The error shows as today; pending edits show their path lines

errorCases.scenario: A check is still running when its diff state is ended
errorCases.detection: abandonTurn cleared the governor's turn, so the check finds the turn it captured is no longer current; the host also sees the diff state is ended
errorCases.response: The check calls nothing on the render seam; nothing is pushed or posted
errorCases.userImpact: None; the held paths were settled when the diff state ended

errorCases.scenario: A followed turn runs while the governor still holds an older snapshot
errorCases.detection: followLiveTurn has no diff state: the holding rules are reached only through the sink of a turn the host started
errorCases.response: The followed turn's rows are written and posted as today and no check is asked for
errorCases.userImpact: Path lines and result rows as today

errorCases.scenario: An edit tool call fails (claude reports is_error)
errorCases.detection: The tool-result event carries editPath and isError true
errorCases.response: The host pushes and posts the held path's marker row, then the result row with the error text
errorCases.userImpact: The reader sees the path and the error, as today

errorCases.scenario: A claude edit never gets a result before the turn ends
errorCases.detection: The path is still held when the diff state is ended, by onTerminal after the last check or by any other exit
errorCases.response: Every held path is settled then: a path with no section gets its marker row
errorCases.userImpact: The path line shows, as today

errorCases.scenario: A codex file_change item names no file (no changes list and no path)
errorCases.detection: The mapper finds neither item.changes nor item.path
errorCases.response: One 'file-edit' event with the path '(unknown)', as today; when settled it has no section, so its marker row '(unknown)' is written
errorCases.userImpact: The line '(unknown)' shows as it does today, beside whatever widgets the check found

errorCases.scenario: The 'diff' renderer throws on a malformed saved row
errorCases.detection: The registry's renderRow catches a renderer's exception
errorCases.response: The row is drawn by the fallback renderer, as for any other renderer that throws
errorCases.userImpact: One plain line in place of one widget

errorCases.scenario: A row's `replaces` names an id that no first row carries (a damaged file, or the first row is missing)
errorCases.detection: pageBefore finds no role:'diff' row with that sid to substitute into; redrawDiff finds no widget remembered under it
errorCases.response: The row is ignored and draws nothing

errorCases.scenario: The private index file cannot be removed
errorCases.response: The governor logs a warning; the next turn uses a new path
errorCases.userImpact: None; a small file is left in the temporary directory

invariantsToPreserve.text: The governor only observes: it never blocks or delays the CLI's write, and the turn loop never waits for git
The user's own index and working tree are not changed by a snapshot or a check
git is reached only through the injected runGit, so the baseline is tested with a fake
A session's transcript is only ever pushed to: no row is removed, inserted or rewritten, so the file store's append-only save writes every row
Nothing saved depends on a row's position in the file, because another window's rows can come before this window's new rows

The turn lifecycle is not changed: a detached, superseded or failed turn still gets no onTerminal, and a followed turn still has only onEvent and onEnd; the host ends its own diff state at those points
A followed turn writes and posts the same rows as today
A renderer of a saved kind builds its node through line(), so the live path, the restore handler and the pager's older-page path all append it
A row that is drawn live is drawn the same way on restore: both go through toViewModel
The host toViewModel and its webview mirror give the same view-model for the same input
A turn with no editGovernance deps, or with diffView 'editor', writes and posts the same rows as today, and the turn-event path and markerFor are not changed
Every edit an edit tool makes leaves a trace in the chat, on every way a turn can stop reporting
The webview writes text with textContent, uses only the shell's theme names and follows the strict content security policy
baseline.read still returns the turn-start content of a tracked file and of a file that was untracked at the start, and undefined for a file the turn created
pageBefore returns the same firstIndex and row count for the same transcript and arguments

migration.stateBefore: On a 'file-edit' event the governor compares the whole file with its turn-start content in process (defaultComputeDiff, one section covering the file) and the host posts 'edit-prompt'; the shell draws a .insrc-term-diff box that the transcript's flex column shrinks to nothing, and nothing is saved. The reader sees the path's marker row and, for claude, a 'file has been updated' result row with a chevron that changes nothing. A change made by a shell command causes no 'file-edit' event and no diff, and a codex patch shows the path '(unknown)'. The snapshot is `git stash create` plus the text of untracked files. The file store appends rows and never rewrites one. A turn that is detached, superseded or fails gets no onTerminal, and a followed turn has its own event path (s1 bundles: symbol.locate, the two search.text bundles on events and on the turn lifecycle, data-model.trace, probe).
migration.stateAfter: The snapshot is a git tree written through a private copy of the index. For each turn the host starts in a git folder with the chat view on, it keeps one diff state: after every tool result and file-edit event, and once at the turn's end, the governor asks git for the patch between the snapshot tree and the working tree; the host pushes each new section as a role:'diff' row with a section id and each change or withdrawal as a further row that names that id, and posts every such row as 'transcript-row'. The path marker and the successful edit result row are held back while the diff state is open, and a held path with no section is written after its check. The diff state is ended at the turn's end, a detach, a stop, an error or the next turn's start, settling its held paths and releasing the snapshot. A followed turn writes its rows as today. The window the host cuts carries each section's latest version at its first row's place, and the shell draws it as a folded widget, live, on reload and on older pages. The codex mapper reports each file a patch changed. 'edit-prompt', renderDiff, the .insrc-diff-* rules and defaultComputeDiff are gone.

migration.backwardCompat: No public API changes; everything is inside the plugin. A chat saved before the change has no diff rows and loads and draws as before. The store's files keep their format: diff rows are ordinary lines of the rows file. A chat saved after the change and opened by an older plugin build draws each diff row through the fallback renderer as an empty line, because a row with an unknown role has no text. The insrc.chat.diffView setting keeps its meaning. The turn lifecycle and the follow path are not changed.

alternativesConsidered.name: Git tree diff, appended rows linked by a section id, widget state owned by the started turn
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Compare two git trees written through a private index, save each section as a pushed transcript row with an id and each later version as a row naming that id, and keep the widget state in one object per turn the host starts, ended on every way that turn stops reporting.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The baseline snapshots by copying the index and running `git add -A` and `git write-tree` against the copy; a check writes a second tree and returns `git diff --no-renames -U3 --relative <start> <now>`. A pure module parses the patch and reconciles sections by path and old-line range. The host only pushes rows: a new section is a role:'diff' row with a sid, a later version a row with `replaces: <sid>`; the window cut gives the latest version at the first row's place. Rows the host writes outside the event path reach the webview as 'transcript-row'. The host makes one object for each turn it starts; holding back a path line, asking for checks and applying their results all go through that object. The object is ended when the turn ends, is detached, is superseded by a newer turn, errors, or the panel closes: held paths are settled at once, later results are dropped and the snapshot is released. A followed turn has no such object and writes its rows as today.
pros: One comparison for claude, codex and shell-command edits
Push-only rows, a position-free link, and one message for host-written rows
No state can outlive its turn: a stale snapshot cannot hold back rows of a followed or later turn
Every edit leaves a trace on every exit path
cons: After a chat switch, a panel close or a window reload in mid-turn, the rest of that turn shows path lines as today and no widgets
Every change to a section saves the section again
runGit needs an environment argument and the baseline a temporary file

alternativesConsidered.name: As a1, but widgets continue through a followed turn
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the snapshot alive across a detach and let followLiveTurn pick the widget state up again.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The per-turn object is kept when the turn is detached and is found again, by session and turn id, when the host follows that turn; the follow path then holds paths, asks for checks and applies results as the live path does, and ends the object at onEnd. The object is still ended when a newer turn begins.
pros: A chat switch and back keeps widgets for the rest of the turn
cons: Does not survive a window reload, where the snapshot handle is lost, so two behaviours remain
While the turn is detached another chat's turn may begin and take its own snapshot of a tree the detached turn is still changing
A second event path with the full holding logic, and state that outlives the sink that made it
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Better after a chat switch, but a larger build with a second holding path and state that outlives its sink; it can follow as its own change.

alternativesConsidered.name: As a1, but holding depends on the governor's state
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The second revision's shape: the host asks governor.sectionsActive() on every event and ends nothing explicitly.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Rows are held back whenever the governor has a snapshot and the chat view is on, on every caller of appendEvent; held paths are settled by the check after their result or by the last check in onTerminal.
pros: No per-turn object in the host
cons: A detached, superseded or failed turn never reaches onTerminal, so held paths are never written and the snapshot is not released
The governor is one per host, so a followed turn would be held back by whatever turn the governor last began
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Less host state, but it loses path lines on every exit path other than the normal end.
